SECTION I
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
A. INTRODUCTION
This document describes and assesses the environmental impact of a three-year housing and Community Development Plan for the City of San Jose. The plan has been developed for local implementation with federal funding pursuant to the Housing and Community Development Act of 1977. This program, known as the Community Development Block Grant program, provides funds and administration for a period of three years, commencing in July 1, 1978. The Community Development Block Grant program was begun in 1975 under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974. At that time the San Jose City administration and a citizen CDBG Steering Committee developed the first three-year plan of concentrated improvements in small target neighborhoods. The activities in these target areas included housing rehabilitation, street improvements, and park projects.
B. BACKGROUND - HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ACT
The primary purpose of the Housing and Community Development Acts of 1974 and 1977 is to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing and a suitable living environment, and by expanding economic opportunities, principally for persons of low and moderate income. The Acts provide Federal assistance for the support of activities that will contribute to the elimination of urban blight and the conditions which lead to blight and neighborhood deterioration.
The legislation seeks to eliminate conditions detrimental to health, safety and public welfare of communities through code enforcement, demolition and structural rehabilitation. Conservation and expansion of existing housing stock to provide a more suitable living environment and the expansion and improvement of community services and facilities are important objectives of the CDBG program. The Housing Act stresses the reduction of geographically isolated income and ethnic groupings and seeks to promote the diversity and vitality of neighborhoods in two complimentary manners; the dispersal of lower income housing opportunities throughout a community, and by revitalizing deteriorating or deteriorated neighborhoods sufficiently to attract higher income residents. It is the stated intent of the Act that the federal assistance made available through the block grant program not be used to reduce the amount of local financial support for community development below the level of such support prior to the enactment of the program.
